_doc: Per-repo config for ~/.claude/skills/route-crawl. Requests every page offda9.com serves and attributes any 5xx to the fatal that caused it. Added 2026-09-08 after a PHP TypeError printed into forge.php's body while the page still returned 200 — a status-only check called that healthy.
_route_root_why: The repo root IS the docroot since the public/ -> root restructure (801668f), so there is no subdirectory to aim at.
_excludes_why: SAFETY FIRST, not tidiness. A crawler requests every route it discovers, so anything that SENDS or MUTATES on GET must never be discoverable: api/drip/sender.php and weekly_lovelogic_sender.php mail real subscribers, contact-handler.php and founding_patron_launch_sender.php send, api/soundcloud/set_sotw.php and api/v1/me/settings.php write. Excluding api/ and the senders wholesale is the safe boundary — an endpoint is not a page, and its health belongs to its own smoke test.
includes/ and dashboard/includes/ are partials loaded BY pages; requested directly they fatal on missing scope and would report a fault that does not exist for any visitor.
config/ holds credentials and *.example.php stubs. private/ is the admin area and is named for what it is.
curriculum/_codex.php is the shared renderer, not a lesson; the 16 lessons under curriculum/<tier>/ ARE crawled, because they are the pages the Atlas and the Forge link to.
download.php streams a file rather than rendering a page.

admin/index.php is a ROUTER that forwards /admin/<path> into private/admin/<path>, so crawling it walks straight through the private/ exclusion into the admin dashboard. Excluding private/ while leaving its front door open would have been an exclusion in name only.

email-templates/ holds the shared email chrome (a layout partial included by the mailers), not a page. It was the crawl's only finding on the first run, reported as 'no response' rather than a 5xx because its directory name contains a space — a reminder that a route list built from the filesystem inherits the filesystem's oddities, and that 'no response' is not the same finding as '500'.
_error_log_caveat: This host sets php.ini error_log to the bare filename 'error_log', which cPanel resolves RELATIVE TO THE ERRORING SCRIPT'S DIRECTORY. So there is no single log: a fatal in atlas.php lands in public_html/error_log, one in api/v1/atlas-ping.php lands in public_html/api/v1/error_log. The path above is the docroot's, which covers the top-level pages that make up most of the crawled surface. Attribution for a fatal in a subdirectory route will therefore come back empty even though the 5xx itself is still reported — the crawl still catches the break, it just cannot always name the cause. Do not read an empty attribution as 'no fatal'.
